findings.title: Referee decline link routes to a 404 and invokes an obsolete two-parameter backend path instead of token verification
findings.scenario: Zoe registers as an Explorer and provides a referee for verification. The referee receives an email request and clicks the decline link, but lands on a not-found page because the web router expects two parameters instead of the single email token. Even if reached directly, the decline page attempts to submit separate ID parameters to a non-existent API route rather than the server's signed token endpoint. The referee cannot decline, reminder emails continue to be sent to them, and Zoe is never alerted to nominate a replacement referee.
findings.test_needed: Navigating to /onboarding/referee-reject/<token> with a valid signed token renders the decline page and sends a POST with the token to /api/v1/onboarding/referee-reject/<token>/, returning 200 rather than 404.

owner_question.question: When Zoe's nominated referee clicks the decline link in their email request, what should happen?
options: The referee decline page accepts the signed token, records the decline, notifies Zoe to nominate a new referee, and cancels reminder emails
The decline link asks the referee to confirm their decision on a questionnaire before cancelling reminders
Keep today's behaviour where the decline link fails with a not found error
